page: Microsoft Azure DC32es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon TDX processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 32 vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. It includes support for hardware extensions such as AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 execution, and AES cryptography acceleration.

The virtual machine is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring remote block storage for persistence. In addition, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are allocated by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across synthetic evaluation suites. Stress-ng scores show 1,782.09 for single-core and 28,294.03 for multi-core throughput, while Geekbench yields 1,874.0 single-core and 14,519.0 multi-core ratings. While general compute tests like PassMark CPU score 41,869.94 and Clang compilation sits at 27,134.0, specific tests show elevated execution speeds, such as PassMark physics at 6,458.48 and Geekbench image processing at 14,177.0, both placing in the top quartile.

With 37.03 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and solid database benchmark metrics, the DC32es_v6 delivers stable throughput for balanced production workloads. The absence of local disk requires external storage planning, making it an efficient option for distributed enterprise applications, memory-resident caches, CI/CD runners, and general compute operations.
description: Microsoft Azure DC32es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon TDX processor on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 16 physical cores and hyper-threading to deliver 32 dedicated vCPUs, the server is paired with 128.0 GB of memory, reflecting a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. The CPU features 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX vector and matrix instructions. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and contains no discrete GPUs, utilizing external storage for all disk I/O. Benchmark assessments place its multi-core and single-core CPU throughput firmly in the median tier, with stronger relative results in PassMark physics and image processing. The DC32es_v6 is well suited for balanced enterprise workloads, compilation jobs, caching layers, and general backend application serving.
